items.headline: Spider-Man just posted the biggest opening day in movie history
items.body: The record didn't stop at those preview numbers: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' pulled a jaw-dropping opening day north of $165 million on Friday (previews included) — the biggest single day the box office has ever seen — and it's cruising toward a monster debut weekend around $270 million. Tom Holland's return is officially the movie event of the year.
items.say: That new Spider-Man just had the biggest opening day in movie history — like $165 million in a single day. It's gonna be the biggest debut of the year. You catch it yet?

items.headline: Mbeumo bags two as Man United down Atlético — a stacked day of preseason friendlies
items.body: Real club football is nearly back, and Saturday was the loudest tune-up yet: Bryan Mbeumo scored twice — a cool penalty and a 74th-minute finish — to give Manchester United a 2-1 comeback win over Atlético Madrid in Stockholm. It headlined a marquee day, with Manchester City facing Inter Milan in Hong Kong and Arsenal at Girona, all sharpening up before the Premier League kicks off in a couple of weeks.
items.say: The Premier League clubs are doing their big preseason friendlies — United beat Atlético Madrid today, and City and Arsenal were out too. Season's nearly back. You support anyone over there?

items.headline: SummerSlam is here — Night 1 goes down tonight in Minneapolis
items.body: WWE's biggest summer weekend kicks off tonight with Night 1 at U.S. Bank Stadium: CM Punk defends the Undisputed WWE Title against his old friend Cody Rhodes in the main event, Brock Lesnar and Oba Femi finally settle things inside Hell in a Cell, and Liv Morgan puts her Women's World Title on the line against IYO SKY. Big-spectacle stuff whether you're a diehard or just curious.
items.say: SummerSlam's tonight — CM Punk vs Cody Rhodes for the title, and Brock Lesnar in a cage match. Even if you don't follow wrestling it's a fun spectacle. You ever watch WWE?

items.headline: One day to the deadline — the dominoes are finally dropping
items.body: It's the final weekend before Monday's 6pm ET trade deadline and the market's waking up: the Mets have gone into full sell mode, the Twins scooped up reliever A.J. Minter and starter Dean Kremer, and the whole sport is still waiting on the big one — will Detroit finally deal two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, with the Dodgers lurking? Expect chaos right up to the buzzer.
items.say: The baseball trade deadline's Monday and deals are finally flying — the Mets are selling everyone, and everybody's still waiting to see if the Tigers trade Skubal, the best pitcher around. Next couple days could be nuts. You following it?

items.headline: Ted Lasso is finally coming back — Season 4 lands Wednesday
items.body: After a three-year wait, the feel-good juggernaut returns: 'Ted Lasso' Season 4 premieres Wednesday on Apple TV+, with Ted (Jason Sudeikis) taking on his biggest challenge yet — coaching a second-division women's team back in Richmond. New episodes drop weekly through October, and the good vibes are very much intact.
items.say: Ted Lasso's actually coming back Wednesday — first new season in three years. This time he's coaching a women's team. If you loved it, it's a great week. You watch that show?

items.headline: Caitlin Clark and the Fever are the hottest team in the WNBA
items.body: Indiana is on a tear: the Fever have ripped off a five-game winning streak and just became the first team in WNBA history to score 100+ in four straight games, with Caitlin Clark pouring in 32 in the latest one. They've climbed the standings and now carry the league's best title odds by some models — the stretch run to the playoffs just got fun.
items.say: The Fever are red-hot — Caitlin Clark's team just set a WNBA record scoring 100-plus four games in a row, and now they've got the best championship odds. The league's really fun this year. You been watching?

items.headline: Ariana Grande's 'Petal' is out — and it went straight to No. 1
items.body: Ariana Grande's eighth album, 'petal,' arrived Friday and immediately shot to the top of the charts — her first full record since 'Eternal Sunshine.' It's a rawer, more personal Ari, anchored by lead single 'Hate That I Made You Love Me,' which became her tenth career No. 1 on the Hot 100. A big pop moment for the weekend playlist.
items.say: Ariana Grande dropped a new album Friday and it went straight to number one — her first in a couple years, and supposedly her most personal one. You into her stuff?

items.headline: Football's back next week — and Canton's about to enshrine a loaded class
items.body: The NFL calendar is flipping over: the Pro Football Hall of Fame Game kicks off preseason Thursday (Cardinals vs. Panthers in Canton), and Saturday the Class of 2026 gets its gold jackets — a stacked group led by Drew Brees and Larry Fitzgerald, plus Luke Kuechly, Adam Vinatieri and Roger Craig. Real football, and a genuinely great set of careers to celebrate.
items.say: Football's basically back — the Hall of Fame game is Thursday, and they're inducting Drew Brees and Larry Fitzgerald this weekend. Fun way to ease into the season. You ready for football?

items.headline: 'Lioness' returns Sunday — Taylor Sheridan's spy thriller is back for Season 3
items.body: For the prestige-thriller crowd, Taylor Sheridan's 'Lioness' drops Season 3 on Paramount+ this Sunday. Zoe Saldaña's Joe is squeezed from every side — hidden networks, foreign operatives and personal betrayals all closing in at once — with Nicole Kidman and Morgan Freeman back in the mix. Tense, glossy, binge-ready TV.
items.say: The Taylor Sheridan spy show 'Lioness' is back Sunday — Zoe Saldaña, Nicole Kidman, Morgan Freeman. Good tense binge if you need a new one. You watch any of his stuff?
